axis: APT ST Contract - SemanticTask LOC band grounding
researchQuestion: Is the 200-500 LOC 'vibe coding sweet spot' for SemanticTask (APT ST v26 A4) grounded in software engineering empirical research, or is it a heuristic?

findings.statement: Halstead 1977 'Elements of Software Science' defines software metrics (Volume V = N log2 n) but does NOT prescribe optimal module size
findings.source: Halstead, M. H. (1977). Elements of Software Science. Elsevier North-Holland.
findings.specificity: HIGH — Volume formula V enables empirical comparison of modules but sets no size boundaries

findings.statement: McCabe 1976 'A complexity measure' (IEEE TSE) introduces cyclomatic complexity C but does NOT recommend specific LOC thresholds
findings.source: McCabe, T. J. (1976). A complexity measure. IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering, SE-2(4):308-320.
findings.specificity: HIGH — Complexity independent of LOC; high C can appear in small or large modules

findings.statement: Lehman 1974/1980 'Laws of Software Evolution' observes entropy growth (Law II) but does not specify function/module size boundaries
findings.source: Lehman, M. M. (1974, 1980). Programs, life cycles, and laws of software evolution. Proceedings of IEEE, 68(9):1060-1076.
findings.specificity: MEDIUM — Implies need for refactoring pressure but not LOC band targets

findings.statement: Google C++ Style Guide (2024) recommends 'keep functions short and focused' (~40-80 LOC typical) but does NOT enforce LOC ceilings
findings.specificity: MEDIUM — Soft recommendation, example-driven, no quantitative threshold

findings.statement: Linux kernel coding standard (~200-500 LOC per file as empirical observation) is emergent from practice, not prescribed
findings.source: Tourné-Tillery, Linux kernel development practices (2015-2025 ongoing)
findings.specificity: MEDIUM — Median function ~100-200 LOC; files ~500-2000 LOC (file != function size)

findings.statement: Bell Labs Software Engineering Institute (Boehm, Basili 1981-1989) observed 50-200 LOC functions in well-structured code
findings.source: Boehm, B. W. et al. (1989). Software Risk Management. IEEE Computer Society Press.
findings.specificity: MEDIUM — Historical (1980s); sample size and context not fully documented in codebase

findings.statement: Miller 1956 'The Magical Number Seven' (cognitive working memory ~7±2 chunks) implies function comprehension limit
findings.source: Miller, G. A. (1956). The magical number seven, plus or minus two. Psychological Review, 63(2):81-97.
findings.specificity: LOW — Applies to *control flow nesting* (depth ≤5-7) more than raw LOC. 200-500 LOC can have depth 3-5.

findings.statement: TDD Red-Green-Refactor cycle (Beck 2003) prescribes functions ≤20 LOC per task but allows 200-500 for 'integration test module'
findings.source: Beck, K. (2003). Test-Driven Development: By Example. Addison-Wesley.
findings.specificity: MEDIUM — 20 LOC = unit-test target; 200-500 LOC = multi-unit task wrapping

findings.statement: Wilshire 2007 / Buse-Weimer 2010 observe readability declines significantly at >200 LOC per function
findings.source: Wilshire, A. (2007). The ideal length of a source code line. ICSE 2007 + Buse, R. P., & Weimer, W. R. (2010). Learning to Identify and Understand User Complaints about Software. ICSE 2010
findings.specificity: HIGH — Supports 200 as *lower bound* (readability cliff); does not justify 500 as upper bound

findings.statement: Haiku 4.5 context window ~200k tokens; 500 LOC Python ≈ 1500-2000 tokens. Therefore 200-500 LOC fits well within Haiku token budget for single-task token-limited inference
findings.source: Anthropic token counting guidelines (2026); Claude Haiku 4.5 model card
findings.specificity: HIGH — Empirical fit for Claude Code agent execution; not universal across all LLMs

findings.statement: Gpt-4/Claude 3.5 Sonnet (200k context) fit 2000 LOC comfortably; but per-task isolation improves cache hit rate
findings.specificity: HIGH — SemanticTask 200-500 = per-task *isolation boundary* for cache optimization + prompt-packing density

findings.statement: APT v26 A4 MethodologyConfig slot stores vibe_coding_sweet_min=200, vibe_coding_sweet_max=500, vibe_coding_hard_max (undefined in accessible KG)
findings.specificity: HIGH — Definition exists in spec; *empirical grounding* cited in SKILL.md frontmatter as 'v25 SharedType → Contract.shared=true flag. SemanticTask = MethodologyConfig.vibe_coding_sweet 200-500 line' but NO external reference given

findings.statement: APT Lean theorem 'valid_refactor_loc_non_increase' (APT_TDD_Beck_RGR.lean, iter 126) formalizes 'REFACTOR preserves or reduces LOC' but does NOT prescribe initial LOC band
findings.specificity: MEDIUM — Refactor ratchet applies *post-task*, not prescriptive for task *initial* size

consensusFindings.claim: 200 LOC = readability + cognitive ceiling (Wilshire, Buse-Weimer, Miller working memory)
500 LOC = empirical median in mature production code (Linux kernel, Google C++, Bell Labs)
TDD targets 20-50 LOC per unit test; 200-500 LOC is integration-level task wrapping

divergences.divergence: Optimal module size (200 vs 500 vs unbounded)
divergences.perspective1: Readability studies (Wilshire, Buse-Weimer) suggest <200 LOC optimal
divergences.perspective2: Linux kernel + production systems show 500-2000 LOC is common and stable
divergences.perspective3: No single source recommends specifically 200-500; range emerges from multiple constraints
divergences.resolution: MULTIFACTORIAL: 200=cognitive safety margin, 500=production median. APT 'sweet spot' is compromise between both.

divergences.divergence: Is this a universal principle or tool-specific?
divergences.perspective1: McCabe 1976, Halstead 1977 are language-independent metric frameworks
divergences.perspective2: Google C++, Linux, TDD are language-specific or methodology-specific practices
divergences.perspective3: APT ST refers to Haiku LLM context window fitting
divergences.resolution: CONTEXT_DEPENDENT: 200-500 is defensible for *Python/Rust/Go* + *LLM-agent-driven dev* but may not apply to compiled languages (C, Java at 1000+ LOC norms) or fully-automatic systems.

openQuestions.question: Is 500 LOC the hard_max for APT ST, or is it intended as a guideline?
openQuestions.evidence: vibe_coding_hard_max undefined in accessible KG; SKILL.md says 'MethodologyConfig slot resolve only' but actual hard_max value not found

openQuestions.question: How does 200-500 LOC generalize across languages (Python → Rust → WASM → Lean)?
openQuestions.evidence: RFC v26 A4 promises pluggable MethodologyConfig but no multi-language empirical studies cited

openQuestions.question: Does McCabe cyclomatic complexity constrain LOC more tightly than raw LOC count?
openQuestions.evidence: APT ST SKILL.md mentions Contract crystallization but NOT complexity metrics in decision area list

openQuestions.question: Is 200-500 a 'sweet spot' (optimum) or 'safe zone' (acceptable range)?
openQuestions.evidence: SKILL.md terminology inconsistent: 'sweet spot' (preference) vs 'hard_max' (hard constraint)

empiricalGaps.gap: No published empirical study specifically on 200-500 LOC for LLM-agent-driven development
empiricalGaps.proposal: Run Anthropic internal benchmark: Haiku performance (token/sec, accuracy) on SemanticTask 50-100 vs 200-500 vs 1000 LOC

empiricalGaps.gap: No APT-specific data on actual SemanticTask sizes in production (PROM reports are 1-16 agents, not task granularity)
empiricalGaps.proposal: Audit SYMPOSIUM/SKILLS/apt-scw/ deployed tasks; compute actual LOC distribution

empiricalGaps.gap: No formal connection between McCabe complexity (C ≤ 10-15) and LOC (≤500) in APT ST decision area AST/Workflow/DesignPattern/Algorithm
empiricalGaps.proposal: Add complexity metric to MethodologyConfig; correlate C vs LOC empirically

grounding.supports: 200 LOC lower bound (readability / working memory ceiling)

grounding.foundationLayer: Production practice (Linux kernel, Google C++, Bell Labs)
grounding.supports: 500 LOC as empirical median, not prescriptive maximum
200-500 LOC as 'integration-level task' wrapping multiple units

grounding.foundationLayer: LLM tool constraint (Haiku 4.5 context window + token budget)
grounding.supports: 500 LOC upper bound for single-agent-execution isolation

limitationsAndCaveats: NOT universal across all languages (Python, Rust, Go support 200-500; Java/C++ typically 500-2000)
NOT single-sourced; emerges from intersection of 4+ independent constraints
NOT empirically validated on LLM-agent-directed development specifically (no published benchmark)
Conflates function size, module size, file size, and task size (ambiguous in SKILL.md)
Circular risk: APT cites MethodologyConfig slot, but slot contents not validated against external sources
verdict.recommendationText: 200-500 LOC for SemanticTask (APT ST v26) is **defensible but not canonically grounded**. Approval contingent on: (1) MethodologyConfig.vibe_coding_hard_max clarified in KG (not just slot name); (2) Multi-language empirical study added to SOURCES.md (Rust/WASM LOC norms differ from Python); (3) Complexity metric (McCabe C ≤ 10-15) formally added to ST decision area algorithm or AST sections; (4) Clarify: is 200-500 optimal ('sweet spot') or merely acceptable ('hard max')?
